# Lens: Emerging Market Debt

## Applicable Countries
Turkey, Argentina, Pakistan, Egypt, Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh

## Key Characteristics
- External debt in foreign currency (original sin)
- Dependence on foreign capital inflows (portfolio flows, FDI, remittances)
- Limited policy credibility — inflation expectations weakly anchored
- FX reserves as primary shock absorber
- IMF program probability correlates with macro stress
- Political risk directly affects sovereign spreads
- Hard currency debt = different risk than local currency debt

## External Vulnerability Framework

### EM Vulnerability Score (0-100)

**Dimension 1: External Liquidity (30%)**
| Indicator | Low Risk | Medium Risk | High Risk |
|-----------|----------|------------|-----------|
| FX Reserves / Short-term Ext Debt | > 200% | 100-200% | < 100% |
| Import Cover (months) | > 6 | 3-6 | < 3 |
| Current Account (% GDP) | > -2% | -2 to -5% | < -5% |
| External Debt Service / Exports | < 15% | 15-25% | > 25% |

**Dimension 2: Fiscal Sustainability (25%)**
| Indicator | Low Risk | Medium Risk | High Risk |
|-----------|----------|------------|-----------|
| Govt Debt / GDP | < 50% | 50-80% | > 80% |
| FX Debt / Total Govt Debt | < 20% | 20-50% | > 50% |
| Interest Payments / Revenue | < 10% | 10-25% | > 25% |
| Fiscal Deficit / GDP | < 3% | 3-7% | > 7% |

**Dimension 3: Monetary Credibility (20%)**
| Indicator | Low Risk | Medium Risk | High Risk |
|-----------|----------|------------|-----------|
| Inflation (YoY) | < 5% | 5-20% | > 20% |
| Central Bank Independence | High | Medium | Low |
| De-dollarization Progress | Strong | Moderate | None |
| Inflation Expectations Anchoring | Anchored | Drifting | Unanchored |

**Dimension 4: Political / Structural (15%)**
| Indicator | Low Risk | Medium Risk | High Risk |
|-----------|----------|------------|-----------|
| IMF Program Status | None needed | Program active | Off-track |
| Political Stability | Stable | Uncertain | Crisis |
| Sovereign Spread (EMBI) | < 300bp | 300-700bp | > 700bp |

**Dimension 5: Banking Sector (10%)**
| Indicator | Low Risk | Medium Risk | High Risk |
|-----------|----------|------------|-----------|
| NPL Ratio | < 5% | 5-10% | > 10% |
| FX Loans / Total Loans | < 10% | 10-30% | > 30% |
| Loan/Deposit Ratio | < 100% | 100-130% | > 130% |

## The EM Crisis Pattern

```
Phase 1: Capital Inflows (Good Times)
  → Search for yield, EM carry trade, credit boom
  → Currency appreciation, reserves accumulation
  → Warning: Credit growing faster than GDP, current account deteriorating

Phase 2: External Shock
  → Fed tightening, commodity price drop, or political trigger
  → Capital outflows, currency depreciation, reserves drawn down
  → Warning: Reserve loss accelerating, sovereign spread blowing out

Phase 3: Crisis
  → Currency collapse, default risk, banking crisis
  → IMF program, capital controls, austerity
  → Worst: Sovereign-bank doom loop (banks hold govt bonds, govt guarantees banks)

Phase 4: Adjustment
  → Currency undervaluation drives export recovery
  → Current account swings to surplus
  → Slow recovery, often political instability
```

## Early Warning Indicators

| Indicator | Threshold | Lead Time |
|-----------|----------|-----------|
| Reserves falling > 20% in 6 months | < 80% of 6M ago | 3-6 months |
| Sovereign spread > 1000bp | > 1000bp over UST | 1-6 months |
| Import cover < 3 months | < 3 months | 1-3 months |
| Real FX overvaluation > 20% | REER > 120 vs 10Y avg | 6-18 months |
| Credit growth > GDP growth + 10% | Credit gap > 10 | 12-24 months |

## Red Flags
- "This time is different" — the most expensive four words in EM investing
- IMF program signature ≠ crisis resolved — fiscal adjustment takes years
- Elections can reverse reforms — watch political calendar
- EM data quality varies enormously — triangulate multiple sources
- Contagion is real — Argentina default can hit Brazil, Turkey can hit South Africa
